title: The American Town You Can Only Reach Through Canada
subtitle: HISTORY THAT EXPLAINS THE WORLD

shots.say: Imagine living in the United States.
shots.img: cinematic aerial establishing shot of a small coastal american town on a green peninsula at golden hour, documentary photography, 16:9

shots.say: But every time you visit the rest of your own country, you first have to leave it.
shots.img: empty two lane highway curving through tall green forest toward a distant checkpoint, overcast documentary photography, 16:9

shots.say: Driving through a foreign nation just to get back home.
shots.img: documentary close up of a car at a border crossing booth window, grey daylight, realistic photography, 16:9

shots.say: For about a thousand Americans, this is not a thought experiment.
It is ordinary, everyday life.
shots.img: quiet small town residential street with wooden houses among tall pines, morning light, documentary, 16:9

shots.say: This is Point Roberts, Washington.
shots.img: cinematic wide shot of a small american coastal town with sea and mountains behind, golden hour, documentary, 16:9

shots.say: A piece of the United States that hangs beneath Canada.
shots.img: antique parchment map of the pacific northwest coastline, muted sepia tones, top down, no text

shots.say: Cut off from the rest of America by land.
shots.img: aerial drone shot of a forested peninsula tip surrounded by open ocean, dramatic evening light, 16:9

shots.say: To understand how this happened, we go back to a line drawn on a map.
In the eighteen forties, the United States and Britain argued bitterly over their western territories.
shots.img: 1840s diplomats around a table with a large map, candlelight, oil painting style, dramatic chiaroscuro, 16:9

shots.say: The two nations nearly went to war over it.
shots.img: 19th century sailing warships in a tense grey harbour, oil painting style, moody, 16:9

shots.say: In 1846 they signed the Oregon Treaty.
shots.img: aged 19th century treaty document with quill pen and red wax seal on a wooden desk, warm candlelight, macro documentary, 16:9

shots.say: The solution seemed clean. Draw the border straight along the forty ninth parallel.
shots.img: a hand drawing a long straight line across an old map with a ruler, close up, warm lamp light, 16:9

shots.say: All the way from the Rocky Mountains to the Pacific Ocean.
shots.img: vintage sepia map of north america coastline, muted, top down, no text

shots.say: But a straight line does not care about geography.
shots.img: aerial of a rugged coastline with bays and peninsulas at dawn, documentary photography, 16:9

shots.say: Just below that line, a small peninsula reached quietly down from Canada into the sea.
shots.img: satellite style map of a green peninsula and coastal waters, muted colors, top down, no text

shots.say: The tip of that peninsula sat below the parallel.
shots.img: aerial view of a forested peninsula tip with waves on three sides, overcast, documentary, 16:9

shots.say: By the letter of the treaty, it was American soil. But it was attached only to Canada.
shots.img: a lone american flag on a pole beside a quiet coastal road with dense forest, grey sky, documentary, 16:9

shots.say: And so, almost by accident, Point Roberts was born.
Five square miles of the United States, stranded on the wrong side of the border.
shots.img: weathered wooden welcome sign at the edge of a small coastal town, pines and sea behind, golden hour, 16:9

shots.say: To reach the rest of Washington State, a resident must cross into Canada.
shots.img: stylized road map of a coastal border region, muted blue and gold, top down, no text

shots.say: Drive twenty five miles, then cross back into the United States.
shots.img: documentary photograph of a border crossing station with flags and waiting cars, grey daylight, 16:9

shots.say: Two international borders, just to stay in their own country.
For decades this shaped daily life.
shots.img: a quiet small town main street with a few parked cars, overcast morning, documentary photography, 16:9

shots.say: Children were bused across the border to school on the American mainland.
shots.img: a yellow school bus waiting at an international border checkpoint, misty morning, cinematic documentary, 16:9

shots.say: Crossing into Canada and back, twice a day, every school day.
shots.img: close up of a US passport held open at a border booth window, shallow depth of field, documentary, 16:9

shots.left: a lively small town street with people walking and open shops on a bright summer day, documentary photography, 16:9
shots.right: the same style small town street completely empty and deserted under grey overcast sky, documentary photography, 16:9
shots.say: When the borders closed, Point Roberts became one of the most isolated communities in America.
Water on three sides, and a sealed border on the fourth.
shots.img: aerial of a small peninsula town surrounded by grey ocean under heavy clouds, lonely mood, 16:9

shots.say: And yet the strangeness has its rewards.
shots.img: a bald eagle perched on a tall pine with calm ocean behind at golden hour, cinematic wildlife photography, 16:9

shots.say: It is quiet, safe, and stunningly beautiful.
shots.img: orca whale fin breaking calm water near a forested shoreline at sunset, cinematic nature photography, 16:9

shots.say: Canadians even rent mailboxes there to receive American packages.
shots.img: rows of metal mailboxes inside a small rural american post office, warm interior light, documentary, 16:9

shots.say: But Point Roberts is more than a curiosity.
It is a reminder that the borders we treat as natural are often just lines someone once drew.
shots.img: aerial view of a long straight border clearing cut through dense green forest to the horizon, documentary, 16:9

shots.say: Lines that can strand a whole town on the wrong side, forever.
shots.img: a lone figure standing on an empty shoreline looking across water at distant land, dusk, cinematic, 16:9

shots.say: Across the world, similar accidents of geography created enclaves and divided towns.
shots.img: dark stylized world map, muted blue and gold tones, top down, no text

shots.say: Each one a small story of how the modern map was really made.
shots.img: an old globe on a desk lit by a warm lamp in a dark study, cinematic close up, 16:9

shots.say: The world is not drawn the way it is by nature. It is drawn by treaties, by wars.
shots.img: cinematic view of planet earth from space with warm sunrise light along the horizon, 16:9

shots.say: And by the occasional straight line that forgot to look at the ground.
